title:
Comment of John Bottorff in Docket(s)/Project(s) P-15424-000
Submission Date: 10/19/2026

documents.name: 151632.txt
documents.text:
John Bottorff, Oceanside, CA.
CleanEarth4Kids.org opposes the proposed underwater data center in the Bay of Fundy off the coast of Eastport, Maine.

We ask FERC to deny DeepGreen's permit request.

The Bay of Fundy is the summer home of the North Atlantic right whale, one of the most endangered whales in the world, along with many other whale and dolphin species, like Minke Whales, Humpback Whales, endangered Finback Whales, White-sided Dolphins, and Harbour Porpoises.

There are only 70 breeding female North Atlantic right whales left.

DeepGreen is proposing to use over 20 acres of seafloor, with a second phase at 400 acres to build a data center. This will expose sensitive and endangered marine life to noise, heat, pollution, and ship traffic that will cause irreparable harm.

Noise and boat traffic will impact how whales call to each other, find food, and move through the area, and right whales are at a high risk for boat collisions.
